video_title: REACTION: The NBA Responds to ESPN's Report on the Clippers Investigation

quotes.speaker: Mike Ryan Ruiz
quotes.summary_phrase: NBA denies credible evidence of Steve Ballmer funneling money to Kawhi Leonard
quotes.excerpt: the NBA has not found credible evidence to suggest that Steve Ballmer has funneled money through sponsorship
quotes.quote: ESPN came out with a report yesterday that the NBA has not found credible evidence to suggest that Steve Ballmer has funneled money through sponsorship to Kawhi Leonard. That set the internet ablaze. Now everyone is dunking on Pablo because ESPN is reporting that the NBA is not finding a link.

quotes.speaker: Greg Cote
quotes.summary_phrase: Greg Cote defends Pablo Torre's investigation into the Clippers
quotes.excerpt: I believe Pablo Torre and his investigation. If fans are going to be dunking on somebody, it should be Adam Silver
quotes.quote: I believe Pablo Torre and his investigation. If fans are going to be dunking on somebody, it should be Adam Silver for looking at this with blinders on and making a ruling that serves his and his league's best interest. They want this whole thing to go away. They want it to go away, so he's making the prudent announcement that there's just not enough evidence.

quotes.speaker: Mike Ryan Ruiz
quotes.summary_phrase: NBA is currently negotiating punishment with the Clippers
quotes.excerpt: the league is currently negotiating, they're trying to find a resolution as to what the punishment should be
quotes.quote: There was a report not too long ago, a week or so ago, that the league is currently negotiating, they're trying to find a resolution as to what the punishment should be. They're negotiating with Ballmer, with the Clippers, what the punishments in this situation would be. If we're going to use some common sense, why would you have to negotiate what a punishment should be when there's been no findings of wrongdoing?

quotes.speaker: Greg Cote
quotes.summary_phrase: Negotiating a settlement implies admission of some guilt
quotes.excerpt: if you're negotiating a settlement, you're admitting some sort of guilt
quotes.quote: If you're not guilty, you're not guilty. If you're negotiating a settlement, you're admitting some sort of guilt, I would think. It doesn't mean that Pablo Torre was wrong. It doesn't even mean that by 5%.

quotes.speaker: Tony Calatayud
quotes.summary_phrase: Clippers immediately used the NBA statement to discredit the investigation
quotes.excerpt: the Clippers immediately come out with a statement saying, see? As if it's all confirmation
quotes.quote: There's a couple of things with this story. Number one is ESPN story comes out and the Clippers immediately come out with a statement saying, see? As if it's all confirmation. And so when Mike Bass comes out, and Mike Bass is the main spokesperson for the NBA, and you can tell sometimes by the tenor of his releases, he's kind of like Pat Riley in that way where it's like, oh, Mike's not happy about this one.

quotes.speaker: Tony Calatayud
quotes.summary_phrase: NBA's quick response suggests the ESPN report contains significant inaccuracies
quotes.excerpt: the story probably contains significant inaccuracies, right? And these are very credible reporters
quotes.quote: Why would they do that? Because the story probably contains significant inaccuracies, right? And these are very credible reporters who were on that ESPN report. But my thing is always this: I always believe reporters are trying to get it right. But their one vulnerability they have is the source. So we had an example of this quite accidentally, right now, a few seconds ago, where Greg said, hey, the source says the name of the guy that did the vote was so and so.

quotes.speaker: Tony Calatayud
quotes.summary_phrase: Tony Calatayud questions the credibility of the NBA's denial
quotes.excerpt: I find that hard to believe based on all the things that we've presented
quotes.quote: I read it before I even saw Mike Bass's statement. I was like, that, I find that hard to believe based on all the things that we've presented and all the things that we still have yet to present. I find it hard to believe the league like, yeah, they didn't do anything wrong. When I read it, I said, you know what it sounds like? It kind of sounds like the Clippers.

quotes.speaker: Mike Ryan Ruiz
quotes.summary_phrase: NBA and ESPN are league partners, making this report fascinating
quotes.excerpt: the NBA and ESPN are league partners. This report comes out from ESPN with some heavy hitter journalists
quotes.quote: What happened yesterday was fascinating. We have to keep in mind, the NBA and ESPN are league partners. This report comes out from ESPN with some heavy hitter journalists attached, too. ESPN is a big deal. And while everyone's getting their jokes off on Pablo Torre, and everyone's assuming the league partner is carrying water for the league and this was all the plan, the NBA comes out with a statement that, from where I'm sitting boys, was a lot stronger than anything they've directed in the direction of Pablo or his report.

quotes.speaker: Tony Calatayud
quotes.summary_phrase: Kawhi Leonard's compensation exceeded that of other stars
quotes.excerpt: Kawhi Leonard got paid by aspiration an amount that was more than Robert Downey Jr., Leonardo DiCaprio and Drake combined
quotes.quote: Kawhi Leonard got paid by aspiration an amount that was more than Robert Downey Jr., Leonardo DiCaprio and Drake combined to never talk, whereas those guys all did the talking on behalf of that company.

quotes.speaker: Tony Calatayud
quotes.summary_phrase: Dactronics paid Kawhi Leonard despite their policy against paid spokespeople
quotes.excerpt: Dactronics paid Kawhi Leonard as a spokesperson when in the 60 year history of their company, they've never paid
quotes.quote: Dactronics paid Kawhi Leonard as a spokesperson when in the 60 year history of their company, they've never paid for a spokesperson and that's part of their whole philosophy. We don't pay for spokespeople. All right. So in both cases, money was paid to this guy to not say any to not do any spokesperson type activity.
